title: What COVID-19 is teaching us about the importance of smell, with Pamela Dalton, PhD

sentences.en: Smell has been called our most underappreciated sense.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉被称为我们最被低估的感官。

sentences.en: When people think about it, if they think about it at all, many consider it an evolutionary relic, something that is important for animals but not for us humans.
sentences.zh: 当人们想起它时，如果偶尔会想的话，许多人会认为它是一种进化的遗留物，是对动物重要但对我们人类不重要的东西。

sentences.en: We tend to think we aren't even that good at detecting smells, certainly not as good as our dogs, for instance.
sentences.zh: 我们往往认为自己甚至连辨别气味都不那么擅长，当然不如我们的狗，例如。

sentences.en: About 10 years ago, a national poll found that more than half of young people said they'd be willing to give up their sense of smell
sentences.zh: 大约 10 年前，一项全国民意调查发现，超过一半的年轻人表示他们愿意放弃自己的嗅觉

sentences.en: before they'd give up their laptop or cell phone.
sentences.zh: 也不愿意放弃他们的笔记本电脑或手机。

sentences.en: But in recent years, scientists have begun to learn more about this overlooked sense and how to gain a new understanding of how sophisticated human sense of smell really is
sentences.zh: 但近年来，科学家们开始更多地了解这种被忽视的感官，并对人类真实的嗅觉有多么复杂有了新的认识

sentences.en: and how it is intertwined with our mental and physical health.
sentences.zh: 以及它如何与我们的心理和身体健康交织在一起。

sentences.en: Now, the COVID-19 pandemic is giving this research new urgency because one common side effect of the virus, even among people with otherwise mild cases,
sentences.zh: 现在，COVID-19 大流行赋予了这项研究新的紧迫性，因为该病毒的一个常见副作用，即使在其他方面病情较轻的人群中也是如此，

sentences.en: is the loss of smell or changes in the sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 就是丧失嗅觉或嗅觉发生变化。

sentences.en: Some people recover their sense quickly, but for others, the changes seem to be long-lasting or perhaps even permanent.
sentences.zh: 有些人很快就能恢复嗅觉，但对其他人来说，这种变化似乎是长期的，甚至可能是永久性的。

sentences.en: Why is this happening?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: And what are the consequences for those who are affected?
sentences.zh: 这对受影响的人有什么后果？

sentences.en: More broadly, how important is our sense of smell?
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，我们的嗅觉有多重要？

sentences.en: What are the connections between smell and our emotions?
sentences.zh: 嗅觉与我们的情绪之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Pamela Dalton, an experimental psychologist at the Monell Chemical Senses Center in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是费城莫内尔化学感官中心（Monell Chemical Senses Center）的实验心理学家帕梅拉·道尔顿（Pamela Dalton）博士。

sentences.en: An independent nonprofit research institute dedicated to studying the senses of taste and smell.
sentences.zh: 这是一个致力于研究味觉和嗅觉的独立非营利研究机构。

sentences.en: Dr. Dalton's research focuses on how our emotions and cognitive processes affect the way that we experience smell and how smell affects our emotions and our memories.
sentences.zh: 道尔顿博士的研究重点是我们的情绪和认知过程如何影响我们体验气味的方式，以及气味如何影响我们的情绪和记忆。

sentences.en: She's been called a smell-ebrity, especially because of her work to identify the worst smell in the world, which we will talk about.
sentences.zh: 她被称为“嗅觉名人”（smell-ebrity），尤其是因为她致力于甄别世界上最难闻气味的工作，我们等会也会聊到这一点。

sentences.en: How could we not?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么能不聊呢？

sentences.en: She's currently leading a research team that's working on a rapid-smell-based test called Sentinel to identify cases of COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 她目前正领导一个研究团队，致力于开发一种名为“哨兵”（Sentinel）的快速嗅觉测试，以识别 COVID-19 病例。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Dalton.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天做客我们的节目，道尔顿博士。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure, Kim.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸，金。

sentences.en: Because COVID-19 is top of mind for most of us these days, can you tell our listeners, do researchers know why COVID interferes with the sense of smell
sentences.zh: 由于 COVID-19 是我们大多数人如今最关心的问题，您能告诉我们的听众，研究人员是否知道为什么 COVID 会干扰嗅觉

sentences.en: and is loss of smell a common side effect of other viruses?
sentences.zh: 丧失嗅觉是其他病毒常见的副作用吗？

sentences.en: First of all, loss of smell following a virus has been known before, but it has never been as common or as prevalent as it is with the COVID-19 virus.
sentences.zh: 首先，人们以前就知道病毒会导致嗅觉丧失，但它从未像 COVID-19 病毒那样常见或普遍。

sentences.en: And so we are experiencing a tremendous surge in people, the prevalence of people who are losing their sense of smell, even for a brief period of time.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们正在经历人数的巨大激增，失去嗅觉的人的普遍率急剧上升，即使是短时间内也是如此。

sentences.en: And what it's doing is making them aware of just how important this sensory system is.
sentences.zh: 它正在做的是让人们意识到这个感觉系统有多么重要。

sentences.en: I've read reports that COVID can cause both anosmia, the loss of smell, or parosmia, changes in smell.
sentences.zh: 我读过报道称，COVID 既可以导致嗅觉丧失（anosmia），也可以导致嗅觉改变（parosmia）。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about the differences between the two and describe what you and other researchers have found?
sentences.zh: 您能稍微谈谈这两者的区别，并描述一下您和其他研究人员的发现吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, certainly it seems that anosmia, which is the complete loss of ability to smell, is the most dramatic manifestation of a virus, including COVID.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，嗅觉完全丧失（即完全失去闻到气味的能力）似乎是包括 COVID 在内的病毒最引人注目的表现。

sentences.en: It seems like it's turning a light switch off.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像关掉电灯开关一样。

sentences.en: From one minute, you're tasting and smelling, and the next minute, that olfactory sense is completely gone.
sentences.zh: 前一分钟你还能品尝和闻到气味，下一分钟，这种嗅觉就完全消失了。

sentences.en: And of course, that affects not only your ability to smell, but your appreciation of flavor.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不仅影响你闻气味的能力，还影响你对风味的欣赏。

sentences.en: So if you're drinking or eating something, it's going to taste or have the flavor of something completely different once smell is gone.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在吃喝什么东西，一旦嗅觉消失，它的味道或风味就会尝起来完全不同。

sentences.en: At that point, however, it turns out that people are not always aware of changes in their sense of smell unless it is completely gone.
sentences.zh: 然而，在那个时候，事实证明，除非嗅觉完全消失，否则人们并不总是能意识到自己嗅觉的变化。

sentences.en: And so studies that have actually measured people's ability to smell objectively as opposed to ask for self-report have found that there are many more people
sentences.zh: 因此，客观测量人们嗅觉能力的研究所得出的结果（而不是要求自我报告）发现，有更多的人

sentences.en: who have an alteration.
sentences.zh: 他们的嗅觉发生了改变。

sentences.en: So, for example, there is a condition called hyposmia, which is a decrease in your sensitivity, which most people may not be aware of unless they were tested.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一种叫做嗅觉减退（hyposmia）的病症，也就是你的敏感度下降，大多数人可能不会意识到，除非他们接受了测试。

sentences.en: But it turns out that a really high percentage of people that contract COVID do have either anosmia or hyposmia when tested.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，经测试，感染 COVID 的人中，有相当高比例的人确实患有嗅觉丧失或嗅觉减退。

sentences.en: Parosmia, on the other hand, is a different condition.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，异味症（parosmia）是一种不同的病症。

sentences.en: It's the ability to smell, but it's the distortion of what things smell like.
sentences.zh: 它保留了闻气味的能力，但对气味闻起来像什么产生了扭曲。

sentences.en: So your favorite cup of coffee suddenly smells like gasoline, or your chocolate energy bar smells a lot like your dog's poop, which is really very disturbing.
sentences.zh: 所以你最喜欢的咖啡突然闻起来像汽油，或者你的巧克力能量棒闻起来很像你家狗的粪便，这真的很令人不安。

sentences.en: However, we think this is actually what happens potentially in the process of recovery of smell when you have lost your sense of smell
sentences.zh: 然而，我们认为这实际上可能是当你的嗅觉丧失时，在嗅觉恢复过程中潜在发生的情况

sentences.en: and the odor system, the olfactory system, is regenerating.
sentences.zh: 并且气味系统、嗅觉系统正在再生。

sentences.en: And there's still a lot to be learned about this condition.
sentences.zh: 关于这种病症，还有很多需要了解的地方。

sentences.en: It's been very prevalent in COVID, unlike prior viral disorders.
sentences.zh: 它在 COVID 中非常普遍，这与先前的病毒性疾病不同。

sentences.en: And so we're really, unfortunately, having a great opportunity to study it and perhaps understand it in a way we never had the opportunity to do so before.
sentences.zh: 因此，不幸的是，我们确实有了一个绝佳的机会来研究它，并以前所未有的方式去理解它。

sentences.en: Now, I mentioned in my introduction that smell is an underappreciated sense and that people don't realize how important it is until they lose it.
sentences.zh: 现在，我在开场白中提到，嗅觉是一种被低估的感官，人们直到失去它才意识到它有多重要。

sentences.en: How does the loss of smell or changes in their sense of smell affect people?
sentences.zh: 嗅觉丧失或嗅觉变化是如何影响人们的？

sentences.en: What are the mental, physical, and emotional results of losing your sense of smell?
sentences.zh: 失去嗅觉会带来哪些心理、身体和情感上的结果？

sentences.en: It's really interesting because people are not aware until they lose it about how much it informs their ability to know where they are in time and space, their environment.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让人感兴趣，因为人们在失去它之前并没有意识到它在多大程度上告知了他们自己在时间和空间以及环境中的位置。

sentences.en: It's sort of the backdrop of everywhere we go and everyone we interact with.
sentences.zh: 它就像是我们去过的每一个地方和与之互动的每一个人的背景。

sentences.en: It's a piece of the fabric of our lives that we just don't appreciate until it's been cut away.
sentences.zh: 它是我们生活结构的一部分，直到它被剪除，我们才意识到它的价值。

sentences.en: So, for example, people talk about feeling disconnected.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，人们谈到感到脱节。

sentences.en: People talk about feeling disoriented or loSt.
sentences.zh: 人们谈到感到迷失方向或迷路。

sentences.en: They hug a loved one and they feel like there's an important piece of the emotional response that's missing, a recognition of who it is that they didn't even realize was encoded
sentences.zh: 他们拥抱挚爱的人，却觉得缺少了情感反应中至关重要的一部分，那种他们甚至没有意识到已被编码的身份认同

sentences.en: as part of their representation of that person until it was missing.
sentences.zh: 作为他们对该人认知的一部分，直到它消失不见。

sentences.en: On the Manel Center website, there's a section about how parents can talk to children about the loss of smell.
sentences.zh: 在莫内尔中心的网站上，有一个关于父母如何与孩子谈论嗅觉丧失的部分。

sentences.en: I know children are not as susceptible to COVID as adults, but those who do get it, is the loss of smell as common among children as it is in adults?
sentences.zh: 我知道孩子们不像成年人那样容易感染 COVID，但对于那些确实感染了的孩子来说，儿童中嗅觉丧失像成年人那样普遍吗？

sentences.en: Quite honestly, Kim, we don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 老实说，金，我们还不知道。

sentences.en: And that's something that we're trying to learn with our Sentinel test because, as you mentioned in your introduction,
sentences.zh: 这也是我们正试图通过我们的哨兵测试来了解的事情，因为正如你在开场白中提到的，

sentences.en: we're developing a very easy-to-use rapid smell test that we think can be suitable for children.
sentences.zh: 我们正在开发一种非常易于使用的快速嗅觉测试，我们认为它适合儿童。

sentences.en: I worked on the National Institutes of Health Toolbox Odor ID test a number of years ago,
sentences.zh: 我几年前参与了美国国立卫生研究院（National Institutes of Health）工具箱气味识别测试（Toolbox Odor ID test）的工作，

sentences.en: and the goal there was to be able to test children as young as three years old in order to be able to assess their ability to smell.
sentences.zh: 那里的目标是能够测试年仅三岁的儿童，以便评估他们的嗅觉能力。

sentences.en: And this was, irregardless of virus, just sort of understanding the natural ability to smell
sentences.zh: 这与病毒无关，只是一种了解天生嗅觉能力的方式

sentences.en: the same way you would test a child's hearing or their vision, because it is an important sensory system.
sentences.zh: 就像你测试孩子的听力或视力一样，因为它是一个重要的感觉系统。

sentences.en: And so we don't really know what the prevalence is among children, but we do know that children may experience their worlds very differently if they lose their sense of smell,
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的不知道儿童中的普遍率是多少，但我们确实知道，如果孩子们失去嗅觉，他们体验世界的方式可能会非常不同，

sentences.en: and they may not have the language to communicate what that feels like.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能没有语言来表达那种感觉是什么样的。

sentences.en: But probably prior to viral disorders and post-viral olfactory dysfunction, the most common way for children to lose their sense of smell would be following a head injury,
sentences.zh: 但在病毒性疾病和病毒感染后嗅觉功能障碍之前，儿童失去嗅觉最常见的方式可能是头部受伤之后，

sentences.en: a sports-related head injury or something like that.
sentences.zh: 与运动相关的头部受伤或类似的事情。

sentences.en: And so that was really the only cases where we actually had a sense of prevalence.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是我们唯一能够了解其普遍率的病例。

sentences.en: And there, it turned out that the sense of smell was actually pretty, how quickly it returned or whether you lost it,
sentences.zh: 在那里，事实证明，嗅觉实际上相当……它的恢复速度有多快或者你是否失去了它，

sentences.en: actually was pretty indicative of how serious the head injury was.
sentences.zh: 实际上很好地预示了头部受伤的严重程度。

sentences.en: Post-virally, we're really still learning.
sentences.zh: 对于病毒感染后，我们其实仍在学习中。

sentences.en: I'm intrigued by the idea you mentioned a little while ago of the fact that you can measure how acute people's sense of smell is and if it changes over time.
sentences.zh: 我对你刚才提到的一个观点很感兴趣，那就是你可以测量人们的嗅觉有多敏锐，以及它是否会随时间改变。

sentences.en: I mean, we're all used to taking eye tests.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都习惯了做视力测试。

sentences.en: We take hearing tests.
sentences.zh: 我们做听力测试。

sentences.en: You know, there are things that I think are sort of baselines that everybody agrees the E is facing left or right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些我认为是每个人都同意的基准，比如字母 E 的开口朝左还是朝右。

sentences.en: We know how many decibels that sound is that's coming into our right ear.
sentences.zh: 我们知道进入我们右耳的声音有多少分贝。

sentences.en: But how do you measure the degree of taste that someone is experiencing?
sentences.zh: 但是你如何衡量某人正在体验的味觉或嗅觉程度呢？

sentences.en: In a laboratory, in a research setting, you would probably measure what their threshold is for detection.
sentences.zh: 在实验室里，在研究环境中，你可能会测量他们对检测的阈值是什么。

sentences.en: Presenting them the same way, you would decrease the size of the letters on an eye chart or you would decrease the decibels.
sentences.zh: 以同样的方式呈现它们，你会减小视力表上字母的大小或减小分贝。

sentences.en: You would decrease the concentration of a chemical and you would ask them at what point they could detect it.
sentences.zh: 你会降低化学物质的浓度，并询问他们在哪个点可以检测到它。

sentences.en: And there are different ways to do that.
sentences.zh: 有不同的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: That takes a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 这需要很多时间。

sentences.en: It's quite involved.
sentences.zh: 这相当复杂。

sentences.en: It would be done, especially for clinical purposes, if someone came in and said, I lost my sense of smell and you would want to evaluate that.
sentences.zh: 这将会被执行，特别是为了临床目的，如果有人进来并说我失去了嗅觉，你会想要评估这一点。

sentences.en: But in a rapid screening test, there are other ways to get at that information quickly.
sentences.zh: 但在快速筛查测试中，还有其他方法可以快速获取这些信息。

sentences.en: And then if you find a problem, you can refer someone for that more involved kind of testing.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果你发现问题，你可以将某人转诊进行那种更复杂的测试。

sentences.en: But it basically follows the same sensory changes that you would use.
sentences.zh: 但它基本上遵循你会使用的相同的感官变化。

sentences.en: It's a field called psychophysics that is used in vision and hearing as well.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被称为心理物理学（psychophysics）的领域，它也被应用于视觉和听力。

sentences.en: It's just done with odorants instead of letters or sounds.
sentences.zh: 它只是用气味剂代替了字母或声音。

sentences.en: Most patients' sense of smell does seem to come back eventually, I understand.
sentences.zh: 据我所了解，大多数患者的嗅觉最终似乎都会恢复。

sentences.en: But for those who have long-lasting effects, is there hope?
sentences.zh: 但对于那些有持久影响的人来说，还有希望吗？

sentences.en: Are there treatments that you can use to help people regain their sense of smell?
sentences.zh: 有什么治疗方法可以用来帮助人们恢复嗅觉吗？

sentences.en: And can you train yourself to smell again?
sentences.zh: 你可以训练自己重新闻到气味吗？

sentences.en: There is some hope.
sentences.zh: 还是有一些希望的。

sentences.en: It turns out that at least with COVID, most people do recover their sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，至少对于 COVID 而言，大多数人确实恢复了嗅觉。

sentences.en: Sometimes even in a week or two following the initial other symptoms or their positive diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至在出现其他初始症状或确诊后的短短一两周内就会恢复。

sentences.en: Some take up to two to three months.
sentences.zh: 有些人需要长达两到三个月的时间。

sentences.en: And during that period of time, their ability to smell might fluctuate.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他们的嗅觉可能会波动。

sentences.en: They'll smell something and then it'll go away.
sentences.zh: 他们会闻到某种气味，然后它又消失了。

sentences.en: And then one day they'll have a good sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天他们会有很好的嗅觉。

sentences.en: The next day not.
sentences.zh: 第二天又没有了。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, it looks like about maybe 10% of people who have been diagnosed with COVID and who have lost their sense of smell, it persists for longer.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，看起来大约 10% 被诊断患有 COVID 并失去嗅觉的人，这种情况持续的时间更长。

sentences.en: Now, in other post-viral olfactory disorders, if you follow people out long enough, it looks like you can still recover even up to two to three years after you've lost it.
sentences.zh: 现在，在其他病毒感染后的嗅觉障碍中，如果你对人们进行足够长时间的跟踪随访，看起来你甚至可以在失去嗅觉两到三年后仍然恢复。

sentences.en: You may not recover completely, you may not be back to where you started, but you might have enough of a functioning sense of smell to navigate your world and to enjoy food again.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会完全恢复，你可能回不到起点，但你可能会有足够正常运转的嗅觉来在你的世界中穿行并再次享受食物。

sentences.en: So, we are trying to sort of jumpstart that process.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正试图启动这个过程。

sentences.en: And that's one thing that olfactory training is intended to be used for.
sentences.zh: 这也是嗅觉训练（olfactory training）旨在发挥作用的一个方面。

sentences.en: That instead of avoiding smelling things because you can't smell, you actually stimulate your system with four or five different odorants that you smell religiously every day,
sentences.zh: 与其因为闻不到气味而避免闻东西，不如实际上用四五种不同的气味剂来刺激你的系统，你每天虔诚地去闻它们，

sentences.en: a couple of times a day.
sentences.zh: 一天几次。

sentences.en: Sometimes you think about what the odor smelled like when you could remember it.
sentences.zh: 有时你会回想当你能记住它时气味是什么样的。

sentences.en: Sometimes you look at a picture.
sentences.zh: 有时你会看一张图片。

sentences.en: There's different ways to do it.
sentences.zh: 有不同的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But the idea is the more you stimulate the olfactory system, the more you might actually regrow or regenerate the capacity that you had before.
sentences.zh: 但这个想法是，你对嗅觉系统刺激得越多，你就越有可能重新生长或恢复你以前的能力。

sentences.en: So, does that mean that there are cells that are lost that can grow back?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否意味着有些细胞丢失了但可以重新生长？

sentences.en: Is that what's happening physically?
sentences.zh: 这在生理上是正在发生的事情吗？

sentences.en: It depends on the virus.
sentences.zh: 这取决于病毒。

sentences.en: Some viruses appear to actually affect the receptors themselves.
sentences.zh: 一些病毒似乎实际上影响了受体本身。

sentences.en: It appears that in COVID, in a study that was done by Dr. Bob Dada at Harvard, that what gets disrupted by the virus are the supporting cells,
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学的鲍勃·达达（Bob Dadà）博士所做的一项研究表明，在 COVID 中，被病毒破坏的是支持细胞，

sentences.en: the ones that actually work to produce and feed the olfactory receptors.
sentences.zh: 那些实际上负责产生和滋养嗅觉受体的细胞。

sentences.en: And so, once that base gets disrupted, then you have olfactory receptors that turn over.
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦这个基础被破坏，你就会有不断更新的嗅觉受体。

sentences.en: Olfactory receptors have a short lifespan.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉受体寿命很短。

sentences.en: They regenerate continuously throughout life.
sentences.zh: 它们在整个生命过程中不断再生。

sentences.en: But if the architecture isn't there to help them regenerate, then you're going to have a loss.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有架构来帮助它们再生，那么你就会遭受损失。

sentences.en: And so, that's the current main hypothesis of how COVID is disrupting the olfactory system.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是目前关于 COVID 如何破坏嗅觉系统的主要假设。

sentences.en: Once the virus is no longer affecting those supporting cells, they may regenerate.
sentences.zh: 一旦病毒不再影响这些支持细胞，它们可能会再生。

sentences.en: And then the olfactory receptors can start regrowing their connections to be able to allow us to experience what is smelling it.
sentences.zh: 然后嗅觉受体可以开始重新生长它们的连接，从而让我们体验到闻到的是什么。

sentences.en: So, you're working on an NIH-funded initiative to develop a rapid smell test to identify COVID cases.
sentences.zh: 所以，你正在从事一项由美国国立卫生研究院资助的倡议，旨在开发一种快速嗅觉测试来识别 COVID 病例。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: And why would a smell test be better than the test that we have right now?
sentences.zh: 为什么嗅觉测试会比我们现在拥有的测试更好？

sentences.en: Well, we can't say that it's better than an actual diagnostic test, like a nasal swab or an antigen test or a saliva teSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不能说它比实际的诊断测试更好，比如鼻拭子、抗原测试或唾液测试。

sentences.en: But it certainly seems to be better than the symptom screening that people are doing or the temperature screening that people are doing in order to return to the workplace or go into a building or a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 但它肯定看起来比人们为了重返工作岗位、进入建筑物或餐馆而正在进行的症状筛查或体温筛查要好。

sentences.en: I mean, every restaurant I go to in Philadelphia takes my temperature before I go in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在费城去的每一家餐馆在我进去之前都会测量我的体温。

sentences.en: And yet, we know from thousands and hundreds of thousands of instances that this is a very unlikely way to pick up a positive COVID test case.
sentences.zh: 然而，从成千上万甚至数十万个实例中我们知道，这是一种检测出阳性 COVID 测试病例的极不可靠的方法。

sentences.en: And so, given that there have been studies done by this international group of researchers, of which many people at Monell are a part, but worldwide,
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于这群国际研究人员已经进行了研究（莫内尔中心的许多人也是其中一部分，但这是全球性的），

sentences.en: we know that the sense of smell, the loss of sense of smell, is actually more predictive than a fever,
sentences.zh: 我们知道嗅觉，嗅觉的丧失，实际上比发烧更能预测病情，

sentences.en: especially in the early stages of COVID infection, when you might not have a fever yet or you might not have any other symptoms,
sentences.zh: 特别是在 COVID 感染的早期阶段，当时你可能还没有发烧，或者你可能没有任何其他症状，

sentences.en: but you might be infectious, you might be capable of transmitting the virus to someone else.
sentences.zh: 但你可能具有传染性，你可能能够将病毒传播给其他人。

sentences.en: And so, for that reason, we think it has more value as a screening teSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，出于这个原因，我们认为它作为一种筛查测试具有更高的价值。

sentences.en: Now, of course, it can be paired with fever temperature screening and symptom screening as well, but we think it will be, in the long run, as a suite of assessments,
sentences.zh: 当然，它可以与发烧体温筛查和症状筛查相结合，但从长远来看，我们认为它将作为一系列评估，

sentences.en: a better way to identify people who may have COVID, but who are otherwise asymptomatic.
sentences.zh: 成为识别可能患有 COVID 但没有其他症状的人的更好方法。

sentences.en: What might this look like?
sentences.zh: 这会是什么样子的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, we know what these swabs are, and we've seen the guns that they point at your head to point at your temperature, but how will they test your smell?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们知道这些拭子是什么样的，我们也见过他们指着你头部来测量体温的枪，但他们将如何测试你的嗅觉？

sentences.en: Well, what we have is a card.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们有的是一张卡片。

sentences.en: It's a single card, about five by seven, and there are three patches on it.
sentences.zh: 这是一张单张卡片，大约五乘七英寸，上面有三个贴片。

sentences.en: Each one of them is sort of a glue, but only one of them has an odor embedded in the glue,
sentences.zh: 它们中的每一个都有点像胶水，但其中只有一种的胶水里嵌入了气味，

sentences.en: and it's covered by a little plastic screen that you lift up, so you don't have to scratch it.
sentences.zh: 而且它上面覆盖着一层你可以掀起的小塑料薄膜，这样你就不用把它刮坏了。

sentences.en: Many smell testers scratch and sniff, and while they're very good in a controlled environment, the intensity of the odor depends on how you scratch it.
sentences.zh: 许多嗅觉测试需要刮开并闻味，虽然它们在受控环境中效果很好，但气味强度取决于你刮的方式。

sentences.en: You have to have something to scratch it with, and so we were thinking practically about somebody going into an office where there might be 400 people entering,
sentences.zh: 你必须用某种东西来刮开它，所以我们在实际应用中考虑过，比如某人走进一间可能有400人进入的办公室，

sentences.en: you know, at 8.30 in the morning, something that could be done very quickly.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在早上8点30分，需要一种能非常快完成的方法。

sentences.en: So you lift the screen on each of these three patches, and first of all, you scan the QR code with a smartphone, and that brings you to a little survey on your phone.
sentences.zh: 所以你揭开这三个测试贴纸上的每一层薄膜，首先用智能手机扫描二维码，这会引导你进入手机上的一个小调查。

sentences.en: You lift the patches, you smell each one, and you tell us which one has the strongest odor, because the glue has a little bit of odor.
sentences.zh: 你揭开贴纸，分别闻一下，然后告诉我们哪一个气味最强，因为胶水本身带有一点气味。

sentences.en: We're trying to work on that.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力改进这一点。

sentences.en: Then you tell us how strong it is, and that's another really important indicator of COVID, because you may not lose your sense of smell completely,
sentences.zh: 然后你告诉我们气味的强度，这是新冠病毒的另一个非常重要的指标，因为你可能不会完全失去嗅觉，

sentences.en: but something that smelled, let's say, on a 0 to 100 scale yesterday as an 80, all of a sudden smells like a 20 to you, something has changed, right?
sentences.zh: 但是昨天在0到100的量表上闻起来可能是80分的气味，突然对你来说只剩下20分了，这说明情况变了，对吧？

sentences.en: And so then the final question is, what does it smell like?
sentences.zh: 所以最后的那个问题是，它闻起来像什么？

sentences.en: And your smartphone shows you four pictures with labels, and you have to decide which one it is.
sentences.zh: 你的智能手机会向你展示四张带有标签的图片，你必须决定到底是哪一种。

sentences.en: So basically, we're trying to test all three different functions of the way we use our sense of smell in one rapid teSt.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，我们正试图在一项快速测试中，检验我们使用嗅觉的三种不同功能。

sentences.en: And this can be done within two minutes for the first time you've used it, and probably less than a minute on subsequent times.
sentences.zh: 如果是第一次使用，这可以在两分钟内完成，而在随后的使用中可能不到一分钟。

sentences.en: So the throughput is pretty rapid, and we're hopeful that the people that are using it will find it to be equally as convenient.
sentences.zh: 因此测试的吞吐量相当快，我们希望使用它的人也会觉得同样便捷。

sentences.en: There's been a lot written about dogs that can sniff out cancer and other diseases.
sentences.zh: 关于能嗅出癌症和其他疾病的狗，已经有很多报道了。

sentences.en: And a couple of years ago, there was a spate of news stories about a woman in Scotland who could tell whether someone had Parkinson's disease by smelling their T-shirts.
sentences.zh: 几年前，有大量新闻报道称苏格兰有一位女性，通过闻T恤就能辨别一个人是否患有帕金森病。

sentences.en: How much does science know at this point about the smell of particular diseases, and how might that knowledge help in diagnosis and treatment?
sentences.zh: 目前科学界对特定疾病的气味了解多少？这些知识又将如何帮助诊断和治疗？

sentences.en: We think it's very important.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: Back before there were diagnostic tests for a lot of diseases, it was very common for physicians to come and smell a patient.
sentences.zh: 在许多疾病出现诊断测试之前，医生过去常常通过闻病人来做判断。

sentences.en: And actually, there are certain things, like certain ear infections in a child give off a particular odor.
sentences.zh: 事实上，某些病症，比如儿童的某些耳部感染会散发出一种特定的气味。

sentences.en: Of course, people who are in diabetic ketoacidosis have a very particular sort of fruity, apple-y scent to them, which is an important way to distinguish them from someone
sentences.zh: 当然，患有糖尿病酮症酸中毒的人会有一种非常特殊的果香、苹果般的味道，这是将他们与其他人区分开来的一个重要方法，

sentences.en: who's otherwise intoxicated or inebriated, right, because they won't smell like that.
sentences.zh: 那些人只是喝醉了或处于醉酒状态，对吧，因为他们不会有那种气味。

sentences.en: So, moving on to that, scientists like my late colleague at the Monell Center, Dr. George Preddy,
sentences.zh: 那么，接下来，就像我在莫奈尔中心的已故同事乔治·普雷迪博士，

sentences.en: was using sense of smell and the volatiles that people emitted to diagnose other diseases.
sentences.zh: 他曾利用嗅觉和人们散发出的挥发性物质来诊断其他疾病。

sentences.en: He was working with a group at the University of Pennsylvania at the Working Dog Center to diagnose early-stage ovarian cancer, which, as you may know,
sentences.zh: 他当时正与宾夕法尼亚大学工作犬中心的团队合作，诊断早期卵巢癌，你可能也知道，

sentences.en: is something that usually does not get diagnosed until late stages.
sentences.zh: 这种病通常直到晚期才会被诊断出来。

sentences.en: It turns out that inflammation from infection does produce an odor in our bodies that anyone, even naive individuals, can discriminate.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，感染引起的炎症确实会在我们体内产生一种气味，任何人，甚至是毫无经验的人都能辨别出来。

sentences.en: The question is, can you now get more specific?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你现在能更具体一点吗？

sentences.en: What is the nature of the infection?
sentences.zh: 这种感染的本质是什么？

sentences.en: Is it viral?
sentences.zh: 是病毒引起的吗？

sentences.en: Is it bacterial?
sentences.zh: 是细菌引起的吗？

sentences.en: And one of my colleagues at the Monell Center, Bruce Kimball, just recently got a foundation grant to actually study that.
sentences.zh: 我在莫奈尔中心的一位同事布鲁斯·金博尔最近获得了基金会资助，专门来研究这个课题。

sentences.en: So, there's a lot of work going on in the diagnostic area of using smell, or at least using the chemical emissions from our bodies under different disease states.
sentences.zh: 因此，在利用嗅觉，或者至少利用我们在不同疾病状态下身体释放的化学物质进行诊断的领域，有大量的工作正在进行。

sentences.en: Now, right now, it's being done with dogs, but the hope is to use the dogs to be able to isolate
sentences.zh: 目前，这项工作是通过狗来完成的，但人们希望能够利用狗来分离出，

sentences.en: what are the actual chemical signals, and then build like an electronic nose or a sensor that can be used
sentences.zh: 真正的化学信号是什么，然后制造出类似电子鼻或传感器的设备来使用，

sentences.en: so that you don't have to bring a dog into an examining room and have, you know, during your physical exam and have him sniff different parts of your body.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不必把狗带进检查室，你知道的，在体检期间让它去闻你身体的不同部位。

sentences.en: But quite honestly, if that's going to tell me something about my health, I'm all for it.
sentences.zh: 但坦白说，如果这能告诉我一些关于健康的信息，我完全赞成。

sentences.en: That's okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没关系，是的。

sentences.en: It's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: You know, it kind of works both ways.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在某种程度上是双向的。

sentences.en: I had a vet a couple of years ago who wanted to decide whether my dog needed oral surgery and smelled her mouth.
sentences.zh: 几年前我有一位兽医，她想决定我的狗是否需要做口腔手术，于是她闻了闻狗的嘴巴。

sentences.en: That was an important diagnostic tool for her.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，那是一个重要的诊断工具。

sentences.en: She was not trained in the U.S., but, you know, she was right.
sentences.zh: 她不是在美国受的训练，但你知道，她判断对了。

sentences.en: The dog needed oral surgery.
sentences.zh: 那只狗确实需要做口腔手术。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly so.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, yes, that's a really, really developing area of research,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这是一个正在蓬勃发展的研究领域，

sentences.en: and I think it holds a tremendous promise, and it's really one of the pillars of the Monell Center's strategic plan is to build on that.
sentences.zh: 我认为它有着巨大的潜力，而在此基础上继续发展也确实是莫奈尔中心战略计划的支柱之一。

sentences.en: Let's talk about smell a little more generally.
sentences.zh: 让我们更广泛地谈谈嗅觉。

sentences.en: How well do scientists understand how our olfactory system works compared with, say, our visual or auditory systems?
sentences.zh: 与视觉或听觉系统相比，科学家对我们的嗅觉系统运作方式的理解达到了什么程度？

sentences.en: What are the big questions that are unanswered?
sentences.zh: 有哪些尚未解答的重大问题？

sentences.en: Well, we learned a lot going back around 15, 18 years ago when the smell receptor, the ability to smell the receptor, was actually cloned and identified.
sentences.zh: 嗯，回顾大约15、18年前，当嗅觉受体——即嗅觉受体的能力——被真正克隆和识别时，我们学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: I can say that the sense of smell is the last sensory system to give up its secrets to science.
sentences.zh: 可以说，嗅觉是最后一个向科学界交出其秘密的感官系统。

sentences.en: It was very elusive for a very long period of time, and some of that was the difficulty in actually using scent to teSt.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，它都非常难以捉摸，部分原因在于实际使用气味进行测试的难度。

sentences.en: I mean, it's always been something of a niche science, which was partly what attracted me to it to begin with,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它一直是一门小众科学，这也是最初吸引我加入的原因之一，

sentences.en: is that there were so many unanswered questions that I found myself not almost knowing which way to turn, which was a good thing for a young scientist 28 years ago.
sentences.zh: 因为有太多未解之谜，让我发现自己几乎不知该从何下手，对于28年前的一位年轻科学家来说，这倒是一件好事。

sentences.en: But now, what really is the major outstanding questions is how do all these receptors work together and tell our brain what we're smelling?
sentences.zh: 但现在，真正重大的悬而未决的问题是，所有这些受体是如何协同工作并告诉我们的大脑我们在闻什么的？

sentences.en: We know that we can discriminate probably hundreds of thousands of different scents, and we do so with about 400 different types of receptors that combine in different ways
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们大概能辨别几十万种不同的气味，我们通过大约400种不同类型的受体来做到这一点，它们以不同的方式组合，

sentences.en: to send a signal to our brain that tells us we're smelling this blend of coffee versus that blend of coffee.
sentences.zh: 向我们的大脑发送信号，告诉我们我们闻到的是这种咖啡混合豆，还是那种咖啡混合豆。

sentences.en: I mean, really fine-grained discriminations.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是非常细致的辨别。

sentences.en: We still don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我们依然无法理解。

sentences.en: The visual world and the auditory world work in two or three dimensions.
sentences.zh: 视觉世界和听觉世界是在二维或三维空间中运作的。

sentences.en: Smell might work in many more dimensions than that, and we're still trying to figure out.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉可能在更多的维度上运作，我们仍在努力弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: So, for example, at this point in time, it's still unknown if you take a chemical structure that is novel, how will it smell?
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，目前为止，如果你拿一个新颖的化学结构，它闻起来会是什么样，仍然是未知的。

sentences.en: In the same way that you could look at something, you know, on the hue or saturation, you know,
sentences.zh: 就像你可以观察某种东西，你知道的，关于色调或饱和度，你知道的，

sentences.en: the color wheel and predict what it will look like to someone who has normal color vision.
sentences.zh: 色轮，并预测色觉正常的人会看到它是什么颜色。

sentences.en: So, we're really at the beginning of that, and a lot of my colleagues are really working very hard on that, but it is a very complex system.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的才刚刚起步，我的许多同事也在为此付出巨大努力，但这确实是一个非常复杂的系统。

sentences.en: It's much more complex than vision or hearing, and so it's moving more slowly, but it is moving.
sentences.zh: 它比视觉或听觉复杂得多，所以进展较慢，但它确实在前进。

sentences.en: I mean, the ultimate goal, of course, is to be able to digitize smell so that we can transmit a smell
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，终极目标当然是能够将气味数字化，以便我们能够传输气味，

sentences.en: over our computers the same way we could, but we have to know how to create that smell.
sentences.zh: 通过我们的电脑，就像我们可以传输其他东西一样，但我们必须知道如何创造那种气味。

sentences.en: What are the components other than just putting a bunch of different molecules in a box next to your nose and trying to blend them?
sentences.zh: 除了把一堆不同的分子放进你鼻子旁边的盒子里并试图将它们混合之外，还有什么成分？

sentences.en: You know, are there more sophisticated ways of actually digitizing smell the same way we can do with hearing, with noises and also visual stimuli?
sentences.zh: 你知道，有没有更复杂的方法来真正将气味数字化，就像我们对待听觉、噪音以及视觉刺激那样？

sentences.en: I recently saw a report about a 3D printer that was making meat, and I would imagine that smell would be really important,
sentences.zh: 我最近看到一篇关于3D打印肉类的报道，我想嗅觉会非常重要，

sentences.en: that if the meat doesn't smell like meat, and if you cook it and it doesn't smell right, then you're not going to eat, you know, printed meat.
sentences.zh: 如果肉闻起来不像肉，如果你烹饪它而它闻起来不对劲，那么你就不会去吃这种打印肉。

sentences.en: Exactly, yes.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's the same thing that happens to someone who loses their sense of smell, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这和失去嗅觉的人身上发生的情况是一样的，对吧？

sentences.en: All of a sudden, food becomes unappetizing, and that either leads them to stop eating because nothing works, nothing is pleasurable,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，食物变得毫无吸引力，这要么导致他们停止进食，因为什么都不起作用、什么都无法带来快乐，

sentences.en: and they lose weight, or the other side of the coin, which is where they continue eating because they're looking for that experience that they can't have.
sentences.zh: 从而体重减轻；要么走向硬币的另一面，他们继续进食，因为他们在寻找那种无法获得的体验。

sentences.en: So it goes in both directions.
sentences.zh: 所以这是双向的。

sentences.en: So I've read that some people experience a loss of smell after they use a zinc nasal spray, and yet zinc seems to be really connected to the sense of taste.
sentences.zh: 所以我读到过，有些人使用含锌鼻喷雾剂后会经历嗅觉丧失，然而锌似乎又与味觉紧密相连。

sentences.en: There's research showing that people with a taste disorder may see some improvement if they take zinc orally.
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，口服锌的味觉障碍患者可能会看到一些改善。

sentences.en: So how can zinc be bad for smell but good for taste since the two are very intricately connected?
sentences.zh: 既然这两者密不可分，为什么锌对嗅觉有害，却对味觉有益呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, they are separate sensory systems in the periphery.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们在外周是独立的感官系统。

sentences.en: You know, the taste buds and the taste receptors in the oral cavity, of which they are all over our body, but for the purpose of food, we'll talk about the oral cavity,
sentences.zh: 你知道，口腔内的味蕾和味觉受体——它们遍布我们的全身，但为了讨论食物，我们只说口腔内的情况——

sentences.en: are peripherally distinct, but they do combine in the brain because flavor is the quintessential combination of taste and smell, a little bit of texture as well.
sentences.zh: 在外周是截然不同的，但它们确实在大脑中结合在一起，因为风味是味觉和嗅觉的完美结合，当然也有一点质感。

sentences.en: Different chemicals are going to have different effects on different types of receptors, and zinc has been touted as a cure for smell loss,
sentences.zh: 不同的化学物质会对不同类型的受体产生不同的影响，锌曾被吹捧为治疗嗅觉丧失的良药，

sentences.en: and it's also been implicated as something that causes people to at least transiently have a loss of smell.
sentences.zh: 但它也被认为会导致人们至少暂时性地丧失嗅觉。

sentences.en: And so it's currently not recommended as a treatment for smell loss, in other words, inhaling zinc, a sulfate in the nasal spray.
sentences.zh: 因此目前不推荐将其作为治疗嗅觉丧失的手段，换句话说，就是不要在鼻喷雾剂中吸入硫酸锌。

sentences.en: But it is something that people have used.
sentences.zh: 但这是人们确实使用过的一种东西。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem to be very effective, and in some cases may actually cause the opposite effect.
sentences.zh: 它似乎并不是很有效，在某些情况下甚至可能产生相反的效果。

sentences.en: Of course, many people who were using it were also doing so because they thought it was going to ward off a virus or a cold.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多使用它的人也是因为他们认为这能抵御病毒或感冒。

sentences.en: And the question remains, without a clear, controlled study, would they have lost their sense of smell transiently anyway and attributed it to the zinc?
sentences.zh: 问题依然存在，在缺乏明确、对照研究的情况下，他们无论如何都会暂时失去嗅觉并将之归咎于锌吗？

sentences.en: So that's an open question.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个开放的问题。

sentences.en: You've also done research on how smell is intertwined with memory.
sentences.zh: 你还做过关于嗅觉如何与记忆交织在一起的研究。

sentences.en: And a lot of people, I think, have an intuitive sense of this.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人对此都有直观的感受。

sentences.en: We know that certain smells will bring back vivid images of a particular time or place.
sentences.zh: 我们知道某些气味会唤起对特定时间或地点的生动画面。

sentences.en: Why are smell and memory so connected?
sentences.zh: 为什么嗅觉和记忆会如此紧密地联系在一起？

sentences.en: Well, we think partly because of their anatomical proximity in the brain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们认为部分原因是它们在大脑中的解剖学位置非常接近。

sentences.en: That smell is actually part of the limbic system, which is our emotional system that allows us to experience pleasure, fear, sadness, etc.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉实际上是边缘系统的一部分，边缘系统是我们的情绪系统，能让我们体验快乐、恐惧、悲伤等。

sentences.en: And also part of the hippocampus, which is where memories, especially emotional memories, are stored.
sentences.zh: 它也是海马体的一部分，记忆，尤其是情感记忆，就是储存在那里的。

sentences.en: When we smell something, we often don't identify what we're smelling immediately.
sentences.zh: 当我们闻到某种东西时，我们通常不会立即辨认出我们在闻什么。

sentences.en: But what we have is an association between that scent and a person, a place, an experience, a setting.
sentences.zh: 但我们拥有的是这种气味与某个人、某个地方、某种经历、某种环境之间的联系。

sentences.en: So it's almost the cue that brings us back to that memory in a way that other stimuli may do so, but not at such an emotional level.
sentences.zh: 所以它几乎成了一种线索，以其他刺激可能无法企及的、不那么具有情感层面的方式，将我们带回那段记忆中。

sentences.en: A colleague of mine studied this some years ago as well and showed that even though smells weren't better at recalling a memory,
sentences.zh: 我的另一位同事几年前也研究过这一点，并表明尽管气味在回忆记忆方面并不比其他感官更好，

sentences.en: when people recall the memory that was associated with smell, they described it in much more emotional terms and probably felt much more emotional at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但当人们回忆起与气味相关的记忆时，他们会用更多的情感词汇来描述它，并且在当时可能感受到更多的情绪。

sentences.en: And so we think that the interconnections in the cortex are what is responsible for that immediate sense of a flood of emotion or a flood of a memory when we smell something.
sentences.zh: 因此我们认为，皮层中的内部连接正是产生这种感觉的原因：当我们闻到某种东西时，会立即涌现出一种情感洪流或记忆洪流。

sentences.en: You know, a perfume that our grandmother wore or the scent of a former boyfriend or, you know, the chalk smell of being in first grade in school when they still use chalkboards.
sentences.zh: 你知道，祖母用过的香水，或者前男友的气味，或者，你知道的，一年级还在使用黑板时那种学校粉笔的气味。

sentences.en: Well, before COVID came along, one of the things that you were perhaps best known for was some research you did to determine the world's worst smell,
sentences.zh: 好吧，在新冠疫情爆发之前，你最著名的事情之一或许就是你为确定世界上最糟糕的气味而进行的一项研究，

sentences.en: an odor that virtually everyone would find repulsive.
sentences.zh: 一种几乎所有人都会觉得反胃的气味。

sentences.en: How did you do that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: And of course, the kicker is what is the world's worst smell?
sentences.zh: 当然，最关键的问题是，世界上最糟糕的气味究竟是什么？

sentences.en: Well, we had a lot of fun with that, Kim, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，金，我们其实在这个过程中找到了很多乐趣。

sentences.en: It was something that we were interested in from a scientific perspective because unlike taste, smell does not appear to be hardwired.
sentences.zh: 从科学的角度来看，这是我们很感兴趣的一个课题，因为与味觉不同，嗅觉似乎不是天生固定的。

sentences.en: Our versions are preferences.
sentences.zh: 我们的厌恶是后天习得的偏好。

sentences.en: Babies, you know, human babies, mice babies, all mammalian babies will reject bitter tasting substances at birth and they will avidly lick their lips to get something sweet.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人类婴儿、小鼠婴儿、所有哺乳动物的婴儿在出生时都会拒绝味苦的物质，而他们会贪婪地舔嘴唇来获取甜食。

sentences.en: We don't have any real evidence that there are hardwired innate aversions or preferences for smell.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何真正的证据表明嗅觉存在天生固定的厌恶或偏好。

sentences.en: And so we wondered if there were universal malodors, what would they be?
sentences.zh: 所以我们想知道，如果存在普遍的恶臭，那会是什么？

sentences.en: So we looked at biological odors of biological origin, assuming that everyone would have had experience with that at some point in time.
sentences.zh: 因此我们研究了生物来源的生物气味，假设每个人在某个时间点都对此有过体验。

sentences.en: We know, for example, that there are certain kinds of odors associated with foods that are highly preferred in some cultures and repulsed in others.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们知道某些与食物相关的气味在某些文化中高度首选，而在其他文化中则遭到排斥。

sentences.en: I mean, let's take durian fruit, for example, where the smell of it is just, you know, to most people in Western cultures, really unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，以榴莲为例，对大多数西方文化的人来说，它的气味简直，你知道的，非常令人不快。

sentences.en: But if you grew up with that, and quite honestly, it really doesn't smell that same way once it's in your mouth, but, you know, you have to overcome that avoidance.
sentences.zh: 但如果你从小伴随着它长大，而且坦白说，一旦它进了你的嘴里，气味就真的不再一样了，但是，你知道，你必须克服那种回避心理。

sentences.en: So we looked at things like the smell of human waste, the smell of decomposing flesh, burning organic matter.
sentences.zh: 所以我们研究了诸如人类排泄物气味、腐烂尸体的气味、燃烧的有机物等东西。

sentences.en: I collected hair from my hairdresser and burned that and we captured the odors into a matrix.
sentences.zh: 我从理发师那里收集了头发并将其烧掉，然后将气味收集到一个基质中。

sentences.en: And so we tested a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们测试了很多人。

sentences.en: And what we were most interested in was people from different cultural backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 我们最感兴趣的是来自不同文化背景的人。

sentences.en: And so I had some opportunity.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一些机会。

sentences.en: I was actually working on summer programs in South Africa at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我实际上正在南非参与暑期项目。

sentences.en: And so I took some of my odorants with me down to South Africa and tested people there, both white South Africans and black South Africans,
sentences.zh: 所以我把一些气味剂带到了南非，并在那里测试了人们，包括白人南非人和黑人南非人，

sentences.en: to see if there were differences, you know, culturally.
sentences.zh: 来看看是否存在文化上的差异。

sentences.en: We ended up finding a mixture of scents that comprised both organic decomposition, basically sulfur compounds, and a little bit of human waste,
sentences.zh: 我们最终发现了一种混合气味，它既包含有机分解物（基本上是硫化合物），又包含一点人类排泄物，

sentences.en: because that's a danger signal to most people.
sentences.zh: 因为对大多数人来说，那是危险信号。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe not the smell of your own bathroom, but when you smell unfamiliar human waste, you really, in most cultures,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许不是你自家卫生间的气味，但当你闻到不熟悉的人类排泄物时，在大多数文化中，确实如此，

sentences.en: and this was true especially in places where there wasn't good sanitation.
sentences.zh: 在卫生条件不佳的地方尤其如此。

sentences.en: And I've worked in India on some of these kinds of odors as well as in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 我在印度以及南非都研究过这类气味。

sentences.en: It can be a vector for disease.
sentences.zh: 这可能是疾病的传播媒介。

sentences.en: Now, the odor itself has no health impact, but it is a proxy and it's a warning that there's something there that can be dangerous for you.
sentences.zh: 现在，气味本身对健康没有影响，但它是一个代理指标，也是一个警告，表明那里有对你而言危险的东西。

sentences.en: And so when we mixed those together, we came up with something that we called stench soup, and it really did revolt everyone who smelled it.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们把这些混合在一起时，我们想出了一种我们称之为“恶臭汤”的东西，它确实让每一个闻到它的人都感到作呕。

sentences.en: Is it available commercially?
sentences.zh: 它能在市场上买到吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if you wanted to use it on somebody you don't particularly like?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想把它用在某个你特别不喜欢的人身上？

sentences.en: I am not going there.
sentences.zh: 我可不会那么做。

sentences.en: If somebody wants to reach out to me, that's different.
sentences.zh: 如果有人想联系我，那是另一回事。

sentences.en: But yes, no, we are not commercially providing that to anyone at this point in time.
sentences.zh: 但对，没有，我们目前不会向任何人商业化提供这种东西。

sentences.en: But we were interested to at least see that.
sentences.zh: 但我们有兴趣至少去观察这一点。

sentences.en: And, you know, I did not have the opportunity to test this on a two-year-old child or a toddler who we know is sometimes not at all repulsed by the smell of their own diaper
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我没有机会在一个两岁的孩子或幼儿身上测试这一点，我们知道他们有时对自己的尿布气味一点也不反感，

sentences.en: or even their brother's diaper, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至对他们弟弟妹妹的尿布也不反感，对吧？

sentences.en: So at what point in development does this actually occur?
sentences.zh: 那么在发育的哪个阶段这种情况才会真正发生呢？

sentences.en: And that's something that, you know, we're still very interested in.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们，你知道的，依然非常感兴趣的一个问题。

sentences.en: It looks like there is a developmental trajectory.
sentences.zh: 看起来确实存在一个发育轨迹。

sentences.en: The president and director of Monell many years ago, the former director, actually looked at this.
sentences.zh: 很多年前莫奈尔的校长兼主任，前主任，实际上研究过这个问题。

sentences.en: But it turned out to be that around age eight, children started to mimic their parents' preferences and aversions.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，在大约八岁左右，孩子们开始模仿他们父母的偏好和厌恶。

sentences.en: So there's definitely a learning process that goes on.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一个学习的过程。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Dalton, this has been absolutely amazing.
sentences.zh: 好的，道尔顿博士，这次访谈真的太棒了。

sentences.en: I've really enjoyed talking with you.
sentences.zh: 我非常高兴能与您交谈。

sentences.en: I appreciate your taking the time.
sentences.zh: 感谢您拨冗接受采访。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher 以及其他收听播客的平台上找到《心理学对话》往期的节目。

sentences.en: And please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 请给我们留个好评。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有什么意见或想法，可以发邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 地址是 speakingofpsychology，全部连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学对话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Condayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音效剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理协会的金·米尔斯。
